objective: A frozen exploratory census: loops of three rings (every position of the two contacts on each ring) and of four rings (contacts two apart), every ring on rule 60, every contact reading its first ring's left neighbour (alone or with the right one) so that the loop closes, and any read on its second ring; ring sizes 4 to 10. Does any loop keep every contact binding both its rings at every lag?
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory; H1 holds): of 295,056 closed loops of three and four rule-60 rings, 2,707 keep every contact persistent while influence returns round the loop, each contact reading the chains from both neighbouring contacts; all 31 at size 4 verified on full state spaces; 54 four-ring families persist at every size from 4 to 16; in 2,659 every contact needs the rings it does not touch at recurring lags.
title: A census of closed loops of rings
